name: GRASP-4B
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507: 36 full GQA layers (kv heads 8, head_dim 128) and 0 other layers, per the base config.json.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-02. GRASP (Graph Reasoning via Agentic Solving and Probing) from PKU-ML: a staged GRPO RL run on Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 that teaches the model to explore a graph with neighbour retrieval and to compute answers with a code interpreter. Dense 4.41B (config: hidden 2560, 36 layers, 32 heads / 8 KV heads, head_dim 128), apache-2.0, repo created 2026-04-14, full safetensors shards - a real post-trained checkpoint, not an adapter. flops_per_token_active is set to 8.0e9 = 2 x the base's 4B active parameters, following the convention the catalog's base records use; the base record itself carries no FLOP figure, and the generator's 6x-active default (24e9) is the known generator bug, not a claim about this model. CAVEAT THAT MATTERS: the card's headline number is a 53.06% average improvement over its own base, and that average is dominated by a 7.11 -> 88.57 blowout on RealErdos, where the base essentially cannot do the task at all. Read the table as 'a 4B agent with a code interpreter beats a 4B without one on graph reasoning', which is expected, not as a general capability jump: the one column where a plain frontier model (DeepSeek-V3.2) also appears, TSG-Bench, has GRASP at 85.00 vs DeepSeek's 88.00, and ExplaGraphs 97.00 vs 99.00. All eleven columns are the authors' own harness - there is no external re-run and no held-out third-party set.
